summary: Baileys fork with obfuscated license guard and char-code-hidden exfiltration endpoint
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that embeds code which decodes a hidden HTTPS destination from a String.fromCharCode byte array at lib/Socket/messages-send.js lines 425 and 436. The decoded host is https://fiora.nixel.my.id/, a third-party endpoint unrelated to the upstream Baileys project, reached from within the message-send path. The host string is concealed via char-code arithmetic rather than appearing as a plain literal, which is an obfuscation technique used to hide network destinations from casual inspection. The package also ships lib/Utils/license-guard.js as a heavily obfuscated module (hex-mangled identifiers such as _0x1e6253, _0x1d5468, etc., consistent with javascript-obfuscator output), hiding the logic that gates the library's behavior and its interactions with the hidden endpoint. The combination of (a) an obfuscated license/guard module loaded by a WhatsApp session library that handles authentication credentials and message contents, and (b) a char-code-concealed outbound HTTPS destination wired into the outgoing message pipeline, is the fingerprint of covert data relay or credential/session exfiltration from an upstream-impersonating fork, not of legitimate WhatsApp protocol code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
